text: Kungsängen Golf Club is located in Kungsängen, Sweden. It was established in 1989, when the first 18 holes were built. The club now operates two 18-hole golf courses: the 'Kings Course' and the 'Queens Course'. The club house was completed in 1993. The Queens Course is the oldest, opening in 1991, and runs through forests, featuring smaller greens and a shorter layout. The Kings Course opened in 1993 with 18 holes and was later renovated three years later to meet international championship standards. The renovation included widening the course to accommodate the public, and it now includes natural water hazards with fairways surrounded by pines. The club hosted the Scandinavian Masters, a European Tour event, in 1998, 2000, 2002, and 2005. The first Scandinavian Masters victory on the course was achieved by local professional Jesper Parnevik. Kungsängen is 25 minutes from Stockholm and is part of the PGA European Tour Courses. In 2001, the club hosted the STC Scandinavian International, a 54-hole event on the European Senior Tour.
